# Draft:GambleAware

GambleAware
GambleAware (formerly known as the Responsible Gambling Trust and
operating the BeGambleAware.org platform) is an independent charity
based in London, United Kingdom.
Mission
GambleAware is an independent grant-making charity commissioning
prevention and treatment services to keep people safe from gambling
harms across England, Scotland and Wales.
History
The organisation was originally known as the Responsible Gambling Trust.
The name was officially changed to GambleAware on 9 April 2018.
The BeGambleAware.org platform was launched in 2016 as a public-facing
resource for people affected by gambling-related harm.
Activities
GambleAware operates across three key areas:
* Commissioning the National Gambling Treatment Service
* Public health campaigns including the "Bet Regret" initiative
* Commissioning research and evaluation into gambling harm prevention
The charity funds the National Gambling Helpline (0808 8020 133),
operated by GamCare, which is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
Funding
GambleAware is funded by donations from the gambling industry.
The gambling industry is expected to contribute 0.1% of gambling
losses to the charity. However, as contributions are voluntary,
actual donations have historically fallen short of this target.
Regulation and oversight
GambleAware is a registered charity in England and Wales
(Charity number: 1093910) and is listed on the Charity Commission
register. It operates independently from the gambling industry
and the UK Gambling Commission (UKGC).
